quick_skim.title: Optimal Query Complexity for Ground-State Preparation
quick_skim.abstract: We determine the optimal query complexity of ground-state preparation to trace-distance error $\varepsilon$ when an energy threshold in the spectral gap is known. Let $U_H$ be an $α$-block-encoding of a Hamiltonian with unique ground state $|ψ_0\rangle$, and suppose $|\langleψ_0|U_I|0\rangle|\geγ$ for a state-preparation oracle $U_I$. The threshold lies at least $Δ/2$ above the ground-state energy and at least $Δ/2$ below every excited-state energy. We give two algorithms that prepare a state within trace distance $\varepsilon$ of the ground state. One uses $O((α/Δ)(γ^{-1}+\log(1/\varepsilon)))$ calls to $U_H$ in expectation; the other uses $O((α/(γΔ))\log(1/\varepsilon))$ calls to $U_H$ in the worst case. We prove a lower bound matching the expected query count; the corresponding worst-case lower bound follows from Somma and de Wolf [SdW26]. The respective bounds on calls to $U_I$ are $O(1/γ)$ in expectation and $O(γ^{-1}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ in the worst case. On $(N+1)$-dimensional systems, these $U_I$ bounds are also optimal when the expected or worst-case count of $U_H$ calls, respectively, is $o((α/Δ)\sqrt N)$. Both algorithms use a constant-accuracy spectral filter to construct a purifier, which we then sequentially compose during amplitude amplification to prepare a state with constant overlap with the ground state. The expected-query algorithm repeats the preparation followed by one high-accuracy spectral filter until success. The worst-case algorithm uses filters of increasing accuracy and limits the total number of queries.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Determines the optimal query complexity of ground-state preparation given a known spectral-gap energy threshold, using a block-encoding and state-preparation oracle, with matching lower bounds.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 基态制备的查询复杂度此前未被精确刻画。该文在已知谱隙能量阈值的前提下，利用哈密顿量的块编码与态制备预言机，给出两种制备基态的量子算法，分别以期望和最坏情况查询数达到给定迹距离精度。作者证明期望查询数的下界与算法匹配，从而确定了基态制备的最优查询复杂度，对量子科学计算中的资源下界分析具有参考价值。
